rulings: CF-BOWMANS-BEST-PREVIEW-IS-ITS-OWN-PRODUCT (Drew, 2026-09-06): the 20-card BBP1-BBP20 insert is its own product key `bowmans-best-preview`, in BOTH sports it was packed out in. The Stadium Club host is provenance, not identity, so every target's product segment moves.

CF-A-QUALIFIED-REFRACTOR-IS-NOT-A-REFRACTOR (#1846, af7cb34, merged 2026-09-06): Atomic Refractor is its OWN rung at `:atomic-refractor:`, never a plain `:refractor:` with the word 'Atomic' pushed into the subset. The 80 catalog rows in this product were minted 2026-09-04, BEFORE that reader landed, so they carry the pre-fix shape.

THE CHECKLIST IS 20 CARDS. Fetched read-only 2026-09-06, all three sibling SCC pages serve 20 card headers, BBP1-BBP20, with the SAME 20-player roster (BBP1 Allen Iverson ... BBP20 Tariq Abdul-Wahad): set-30234 (base), set-30235 (Refractors), set-30236 (Atomic Refractors). The '10 cards' suggestion is REFUTED by all three pages.

NO SUBSET CLASH, SO NO `sub-` SEGMENT. CF-A-SUBSET-IS-PART-OF-THE-IDENTITY-WHEN-IT-HAS-TO-BE puts `:sub-` in a slug ONLY when a cardNumber clashes ACROSS subsets within the product. Measured: the 320 rows of 1997 basketball topps-stadium-club hold 240 plain-numeric base cards and BBP1-BBP20; no BBP number appears in any other subset. The three setNames are ONE subset at THREE parallel rungs, so the clash the segment exists for does not exist here and every `sub-bowmans-best-preview*` id in this product is a defect, not an identity.

THE PARALLEL AXIS CARRIES THE RUNG. The end state is exactly 3 rows per card -- `:bbp<n>:base:no-auto`, `:bbp<n>:refractor:no-auto`, `:bbp<n>:atomic-refractor:no-auto` -- 60 rows for 20 cards. This is the same shape #1846 pinned for the baseball edition and what today's reader already derives for these three URLs (verified by driving splitParentAndSubset/parallelFromSlug on the live slugs: parentSetKey topps-stadium-club, subset 'Bowmans Best Preview', parallel ''/'Refractor'/'Atomic Refractor').

THE TITLE DECIDES THE RUNG for a pool row, never the stored parallel. Every entry carries its own title evidence; a title spelling 'Atomic' is atomic-refractor, one spelling 'Refractor' without it is refractor, one spelling neither is base.

THE CHECKLIST DECIDES THE SPORT. The Stadium Club FOOTBALL edition of this same insert (Drew Bledsoe #BBP15) is a DIFFERENT checklist and is EXCLUDED, not dragged onto the basketball roster -- the same host-brand scoping #1846 pinned so Stadium Club would not follow Bowman.

EVERY ENTRY IS A REPOINT, NOT A RELOCATE. 25 of the 30 sit on opaque CardHedge vendor partitions (`1653269830987x...`), which are not identity slugs; the pricing engine reads hobbyiqCardId. No partition moves and no document is deleted, so this list cannot half-move a row.

SEQUENCING: run the SCC re-mint for the three basketball pages FIRST, then the CATALOG list (data/catalog-relocations/2026-09-06-bbp-preview-basketball.json, which moves all 60 rows onto the ruled key), then THIS list. A sale repointed at an address the catalog has not created yet is a sale pointing at nothing.

catalogPlan.note: SUPERSEDED, TWICE. When this list was written no catalog lane read a list, so the catalog half was REPORTED here as a plan for a follow-up. Both halves of that plan are now obsolete: relocate-catalog-rows-by-list exists (#1858) and owns the write, and Drew's 2026-09-06 ruling moved the destination off `topps-stadium-club` entirely. The plan is kept as a pointer rather than deleted, so a reader who arrives at this file is sent to the list that is actually run instead of following a stale shape.
supersededWhy: THE SHAPE CHANGED. The plan's 20 retires existed to vacate bare `:refractor:` addresses its own 20 reslugs then landed on. Measured read-only 2026-09-06, the 40 `sub-`-segment rows it names are GONE (the fold and dedup lanes consolidated them) and the product holds exactly 60 clean BBP rows, three rungs per card, no `sub-` anywhere. There is nothing left to retire.

THE DESTINATION CHANGED. Every row now moves to `hiq:basketball:1997:bowmans-best-preview:bbp<n>:<rung>:no-auto` — including the 20 BASE rows the plan said to KEEP, which were correct only while the Preview lived on the host's key. Leaving them would ship two rungs of a card on one product and the third on another.
THE HELPER NOTE STANDS. moveCatalogRow, never patchCatalogRowFields, because changing where a row lives is a move — and the committed lane uses exactly that.
catalogPlan.endState: 60 rows on hiq:basketball:1997:bowmans-best-preview:*, three rungs per card; ZERO BBP rows left on topps-stadium-club.
